brief.t: One 97 Communications was started in 2000 by Vijay Shekhar Sharma; its Paytm app grew from mobile recharges into payments, and use jumped after demonetisation in 2016. It listed in Nov 2021 with an ₹18,300 crore IPO.
It earns from merchant payments (QR, Soundbox, card machines, online gateway) and from distributing loans, insurance and investments for partner banks and NBFCs. It does not lend from its own books.
Founder Vijay Shekhar Sharma is Chairman, MD & CEO; Madhur Deora is President & Group CFO (he left the board in 2025 but kept that role).
Back to profit: FY 2025-26 was its first full year of profit (₹552 crore on revenue of ₹8,437 crore, consolidated), and Q2 FY27 profit was ₹225 crore.

The RBI cancelled the licence of the separate Paytm Payments Bank in April 2026, after curbs in 2022 and 2024. Paytm's own payments arm, PPSL, now holds payment aggregator licences and got an in-principle nod for wallets in Nov 2026.

timeline.t: Vijay Shekhar Sharma founds One 97 Communications.
Demonetisation: Paytm usage jumps as people move away from cash.
Listed on NSE and BSE after an ₹18,300 crore IPO.
RBI bars Paytm Payments Bank from taking new deposits, credits or wallet top-ups.
Subsidiary PPSL gets RBI payment aggregator licences: online, then offline and cross-border.
RBI cancels Paytm Payments Bank's licence; FY26 ends as Paytm's first full year of profit.

model.how: Paytm gives users a free payments app and gives shops QR codes, Soundbox speakers and card machines for a monthly fee. It earns payment fees from merchants and online businesses, and earns commission by helping partner banks and NBFCs give loans and sell insurance and investments to its users and merchants.
flow: Users pay by UPI, cards or wallet in the Paytm app
Shops take payments via QR, Soundbox and card machines
Paytm earns device fees and payment fees
Partners' loans and insurance sold for a commission

industry.regulator: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for payments licences; NPCI runs UPI; SEBI for the listed company
points: UPI is free for users and most merchants (zero MDR), so payment apps earn from devices, online payments and selling financial products.
Licences matter: RBI's action on Paytm Payments Bank shows how compliance can shut down a business line.
Big theme for interviews: how a payments app turns users into customers for loans, insurance and investing.

network.local: Paytm has big field sales teams that sign up shops for QR codes and Soundbox devices, plus tech and product teams in Noida and other cities.

glossary.Net profit: What is left after all costs and taxes. The company's final earnings.
glossary.Revenue: Total money earned from the business in a period, before costs.
glossary.Dividend: Part of the profit paid to shareholders, per share.
glossary.Attrition: The % of employees who leave in a year. Also called employee turnover.
glossary.IPO: Initial Public Offering: when a company first sells its shares to the public.
glossary.Market share: A company's sales as a % of the total sales of its industry.
glossary.Consolidated: Figures for the company together with its subsidiaries. 'Standalone' means the parent company alone.
glossary.BRSR: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report: an official yearly report on people, environment and governance that big listed companies must publish.
glossary.KYC: Know Your Customer: checking a customer's identity before opening an account or selling a product.
glossary.UPI: Unified Payments Interface: India's instant bank-to-bank payment system run by NPCI. Apps like PhonePe, Google Pay and Paytm sit on top of it.
glossary.NPCI: National Payments Corporation of India: the body that runs UPI, RuPay and other retail payment systems.
glossary.MDR: Merchant Discount Rate: the fee a shop pays on each digital payment. UPI and RuPay debit card payments have zero MDR by government rule.
glossary.GMV: Gross Merchandise Value: the total value of payments that pass through a platform in a period.
glossary.Payment aggregator: A company licensed by RBI to collect online payments for merchants and pass the money to them.
glossary.Soundbox: A small speaker device at a shop that announces each payment received, for a monthly fee.
glossary.Contribution margin: Revenue minus direct costs (like payment processing). Shows if the core business makes money before fixed costs.
glossary.EBITDA: Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation: a measure of operating profit.
glossary.Loan distribution: Helping a bank or NBFC give loans to customers and merchants for a fee, without lending its own money.
glossary.Market share cap: An NPCI limit (proposed at 30%) on how much of UPI transactions any one app can handle.
glossary.RBI: Reserve Bank of India, which regulates payments, banks and NBFCs in India.
glossary.Fintech: Financial technology: companies that use apps and software to offer payments, loans, investing or insurance.
glossary.MTU: Monthly Transacting Users: people who made at least one payment on the app in a month.
glossary.PIDF: Payments Infrastructure Development Fund: an RBI scheme that paid incentives for placing payment devices in smaller towns. Paytm's incentives under it ended in Dec 2025.
glossary.PPI: Prepaid Payment Instrument: a wallet or prepaid card you load money into. Needs an RBI licence.
glossary.Payments bank: A small bank licensed by RBI that can take deposits (up to a limit) and offer payments, but cannot give loans.
glossary.PPSL: Paytm Payments Services Ltd: Paytm's wholly-owned payments subsidiary that holds its payment aggregator licences.
glossary.Postpaid: Buy now, pay later: a small credit line, here offered on UPI with partner lenders.
glossary.Default loss guarantee: A promise by a fintech to cover part of the losses if loans it sources for a lender go bad.

Role knowledge, the company and HR questions

Finance.a: Revenue grew faster than costs (FY26 revenue +22% to ₹8,437 crore; in Q2 FY27 indirect costs fell to 46% of revenue from 52%). FY26 EBITDA was ₹502 crore against a ₹1,506 crore loss in FY25, and profit was ₹552 crore.

Finance.q: What is EBITDA margin and what was Paytm's in Q2 FY27?
Finance.a: EBITDA as a % of revenue. Paytm's was about 10% (₹270 crore on ₹2,648 crore revenue), its first double-digit margin.

Finance.q: Why does Paytm not lend from its own books?
Finance.a: It works as a distributor for banks and NBFCs, earning commission without risking its own capital or needing an NBFC licence.

Marketing.q: How would you win back users' trust after the Payments Bank issue?
Marketing.a: Explain clearly that the bank licence issue was separate from the Paytm app, show safety features, use cashback carefully and lean on 8.5 crore active users' word of mouth.

Marketing.q: How can Paytm sell loans to small merchants?
Marketing.a: Use their payment history on Soundbox and QR to offer pre-approved loans from partners, with simple EMIs; more than half of merchant loans go to repeat borrowers.

HR.q: How would you reduce attrition in a large field sales team?
HR.a: Clear incentives, quick payouts, good training, digital tools for onboarding shops and a visible growth path to team lead roles.

Sales.q: Convince a kirana owner to take a Soundbox.
Sales.a: It announces every payment so he never misses or argues over a payment, works during rush hours, and his payment history can help him get a business loan later.

Operations.q: How would you reduce payment frauds on a merchant QR network?
Operations.a: Strong KYC at onboarding, AI checks for unusual patterns, quick blocking of suspicious accounts and fast complaint handling.

Other.q: What is the difference between Paytm and Paytm Payments Bank?
Other.a: Paytm (One 97 Communications) is the listed fintech; Paytm Payments Bank was a separate bank whose licence RBI cancelled in April 2026. Paytm's merchant payments business now sits in its subsidiary PPSL, which holds RBI payment aggregator licences.

interview.why_us: Paytm helped make QR payments normal at Indian shops, and today 8.5 crore people use it every month while 1.64 crore merchants pay for its devices. After a tough regulatory period it has turned profitable and is growing loans, insurance and new licences. Working here means learning payments, technology and field sales at huge scale. I want to contribute to [your role] as it grows.
ask: How will the wallet licence and Paytm Postpaid change the product in the next year?
How is AI changing the way teams work at Paytm?
What does success look like for a new joiner in the first six months?

gd.t: Should UPI payments carry a small fee (MDR) for large merchants?
gd.for: Payment companies need income to invest in safety and reach; big merchants can afford a small fee.
gd.against: Free UPI drove India's cashless growth; fees could push merchants back to cash.

gd.t: Should fintechs be regulated as strictly as banks?
gd.for: They handle people's money and data; the Paytm Payments Bank case shows the risks.
gd.against: Too many rules can slow innovation and keep new players out.

avoid: Don't mix up Paytm (One 97 Communications) with Paytm Payments Bank; the bank's licence was cancelled, not Paytm's.
Don't say Paytm gives loans itself; it distributes loans for partner banks and NBFCs.
Don't say Paytm is loss-making; FY26 was its first full year of profit (₹552 crore).
